transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

My mind keeps getting stuck on the same worrying thoughts about what I might have forgotten or done wrong, and I can’t seem to shut them off even when I’m not at school. It's just really wearing me out, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Do you feel driven to perform certain repetitive behaviors or mental rituals, like checking things over and over, to try to ease these worries?

Yes, I feel completely driven to constantly reread emails, rewrite my lesson plans, and check my parents' calendars and pill boxes. I feel like if I don't do these things, something terrible will happen and it will be my fault. It ends up taking up so much of my time, but I just can't seem to stop.

Aside from these worries about making mistakes or forgetting things, do you also find yourself constantly anxious about a wide range of other everyday topics, like your health, finances, or minor daily matters?

No, I don't really worry about things like my own health or finances. My anxiety is very specifically focused on the fear of making mistakes or forgetting something important related to my schoolwork, my students, or my parents' care and schedules.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with classic symptoms of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (F42). She experiences recurrent, intrusive thoughts (obsessions) about making mistakes or forgetting things, which lead to a fear that something terrible will happen. To alleviate this anxiety, she feels driven to perform repetitive checking behaviors (compulsions), including constantly rereading emails, rewriting lesson plans, and checking her parents' calendars and pill boxes. These rituals are highly time-consuming and cause significant distress. Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) was considered but ruled out, as her anxiety is specifically focused on these obsessive themes rather than a broad range of everyday topics.
